no containment. The script is hand- and agent-authored — the plan's own trust
inventory says so — and the bytes it names are committed under public/lessons/
and served, so `image: ../secretdir/.env` published a credentials file into the
assets directory. Reproduced before fixing. The write side was already checked;
this is the read side of the same boundary, and it now refuses without echoing
the rejected path, which is what `RefusedPath` already promised.

`_read_json` returned None both when no manifest existed and when one existed
and would not parse. Both read as "nothing is cached", and nothing cached
re-synthesises every clip in the lesson — not a free retry, because re-voicing
is not idempotent: every clip comes back different and every line is billed
again. Three outcomes now, the third loud, and OSError and a valid-JSON-but-
wrong-shape manifest are covered by it rather than by a traceback.

The manifest declared two vocabularies and only one of them was checked against
the assets that use it; `verificationOutcomes` is now checked like
`segmentStates`. Both entry points report these refusals as exit 3 with a
message instead of a raw traceback.

The committed fixture regenerates byte-identically, so none of this changes
what the pipeline emits.
